newsitem.title: DUBAI: UK's Marks & Spencer to open Gulf stores.
newsitem.headline: UK's Marks & Spencer to open Gulf stores.

text.p: One of Britain's biggest retailers Marks & Spencer Plc will open its first franchise in the Gulf Arab region this year, a statement by the company said.
M&S said in the statement, dated February 5 and received by Reuters on Thursday, that it has chosen the United Arab Emirates company, al-Futtaim Sons Co LLC, as its franchise partner in the region.

It will be the first venture by M&S in the region, where the company's links with Israel have so far prevented contact between Arab companies and the UK retailer because of an Arab boycott against the Jewish state.
Gulf Arab states in recent years lifted a decades-old boycott of firms and institutions that deal with Israel, the so-called secondary and tertiary boycott.
M&S said in its statement that the UAE company will operate the franchise in the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman.
The statement made no mention to the Gulf's biggest market, Saudi Arabia.
"A franchise operation in the Gulf is an important step in our goal to be one of the leading global volume retailers," Keith Oates, M&S deputy chairman said in the statement.
"Following a lengthy feasibility study, Marks & Spencer has concluded that the markets in the Gulf offer significant commercial opportunities," the statement said.
The aim is to open the first store in the Gulf by the end of 1997, it added, but did not say in which country.
